comments.text:
It's important to point out, that when Trump says Democrats will most likely never attain power, that this is the wrong term to describe winning an election. It is not "attaining power", it's being elected to serve the people! You're supposed to do what you told those electing you what you told them you would do. You're supposed to serve their interests, as they see it.

Winning an election is not supposed to be about attaining power, and the fact that Trump uses this terminology shows us that he doesn't understand that, or that he doesn't care. Of course, it's hard to care enough to even bring it up. Because we already know that he views it simply as power. I just feel I had to bring it up because I think I remember AOC stating that she wants to help the public, regardless of whether they voted for her or not.

Democracy serves everyone, not just those who agree! I feel like that's going above and beyond, but I also feel like politicians that want to go above and beyond are the ones that should be voted for. As opposed to those who simply see it as "attaining power".

There's those who say it's not okay to Gerrymander at all and even though the Republican's are effectively cheating, the Dem's should stay "pure" and not. 
I think the world has shown us that if you "stay pure" then those willing to play dirty will take advantage of you and likely win. But I also think that it would be better if nobody Gerrymandered.
I think the iterated prisoners dilemma is not worthy here: in competitions the strategy that wins is "tit for tat forgive" which means that you do the right thing until they cheat, then you match them, and as soon as they play fair again, so do you. Any transgression is only done in response to the inciting instance.
This doesn't let them get away with underhanded tactics and minimises how underhanded you become to make that happen.
